title: The Room on the Roof
author: Ruskin Bond
curatorNote: Written by Ruskin when he was just seventeen, living in Dehradun. It captures the local streets, the dust, the heavy monsoon, and the intense, shifting friendships of youth.
whyFits: It is the ultimate Dehradun coming-of-age story. A small room of one's own under the sloping roofs can be the centre of the world.
excerpt: Rusty was a quiet boy who lived with his guardian, the missionary Mr. Harrison, in the European community of Dehra Dun. He felt isolated and constrained by the strict rules of his home, where he was forbidden to mix with the local Indian population down in the bazaar.

But one afternoon, during the hot, dusty days before the monsoon, Rusty broke the rules. He walked down into the bazaar. There he met Somi, a Sikh boy riding a bicycle, and Ranbir, a wrestler. In the crowded, chaotic streets filled with the scent of spices, hot tea, and frying pakoras, he felt alive for the very first time.

Somi found him a room to live in—a small room on the roof of a house belonging to the Kapoor family. It was a tiny room with a tin roof that rattled in the rain, but it had a window that looked out over the tree-tops and the distant blue hills.

title: Rain in the Mountains
author: Ruskin Bond
curatorNote: A quiet collection of diary entries, essays, and poems about the rhythmic cycles of valley rains, mountain birds, and the slow growth of pine seedlings.
whyFits: Perfect for reading when it pours outside your hostel window. It teaches you to love the damp mist, the moss on the walls, and the quietness of the hills.
excerpt: Rain in the hills is different from rain in the plains. It does not just fall; it settles in. It rolls up the valley in great banks of white mist, swallowing the trees and the houses until only the peak of the ridge remains.

The pine needles glisten with droplets, and the sound of water dripping from the tin roof is a steady, soothing rhythm. It is a time for hot ginger tea, for sitting by the fireplace with an old journal, and for listening to the wind sighing through the deodars.

The ferns and wild begonias grow thick on the stone walls, and the moss grows rich and green on the oak trees. To live in the hills is to live in close company with nature, where every rainstorm is a cleaning of the soul.

title: Letters to a Young Poet
author: Rainer Maria Rilke
curatorNote: Ten letters written to an aspiring cadet about solitude, love, career choices, and the slow, internal process of growth. Elegant and incredibly profound.
whyFits: An essential companion for starting college. Rilke's words will remind you to 'be patient toward all that is unsolved in your heart' when things feel overwhelming.
excerpt: You ask whether your verses are good. You ask me. You have asked others before. You send them to magazines. You compare them with other poems, and you are disturbed when certain editors reject your efforts. Now, I beg you to give up all that.
Go into yourself. Search for the reason that bids you write; find out whether it is spreading its roots in the deepest place of your heart.
Most of all, ask yourself in the most silent hour of your night: must I write? Build your life according to this necessity.

title: Night Train at Deoli
author: Ruskin Bond
curatorNote: A short story collection set in the trains and small stations of India. The title story is one of the most beautiful pieces of Indian short fiction — brief, haunting, and deeply atmospheric.
whyFits: The train is how you'll arrive. These stories carry the same rhythm as the journey itself — moments glimpsed from a moving window.
excerpt: I was travelling to Dehra Dun when the train stopped at a small station called Deoli. I had never heard of the place before and I was sure I'd never hear of it again.
A girl came down the platform, selling baskets. I saw her for only a few minutes, but her face stayed with me for years. She had a grace that was natural and effortless.
The train moved on. I never saw her again, but whenever I travel that line, I look out of the window at Deoli station, hoping.

title: The Blue Umbrella
author: Ruskin Bond
curatorNote: A gentle fable about a village girl in the hills who finds a beautiful blue umbrella. A story about desire, envy, generosity, and the small economies of mountain towns.
whyFits: Short, charming, and set in the hills you'll be living in. You could read it in a single evening on a rainy night.
excerpt: Binya was a girl who lived with her mother and an elder brother in a little village above Doiwara. She had two goats, a black one and a brown one, and she took them out to graze on the hillside.
The umbrella was like a flower, a great blue flower that had sprung up on the bare hillside. She had never seen anything so beautiful.
She held the umbrella aloft and ran down the slope, spinning it around as she ran. The villagers looked up at her and smiled.

title: Me Before You
author: Jojo Moyes
curatorNote: A heartbreaking romance following Louisa Clark, an eccentric young woman who takes a job caring for Will Traynor, a former high-flyer left paralyzed after an accident.
whyFits: A story about how unexpected encounters can alter the course of your life, pushing you to live beyond your comfort zone.
excerpt: Louisa Clark is an ordinary girl living an ordinary life—steady boyfriend, close-knit family—who has rarely ventured beyond her tiny village. She takes a job working for Will Traynor, who is wheelchair-bound after an accident.

Will has lived a huge life—big business, extreme sports, worldwide travel—and now he is certain he cannot live like this. Will is moody, bossy, and caustic, but Lou refuses to treat him with soft gloves.
Soon, his happiness becomes more important to her than she expected. A deeply emotional tale of two people who couldn't be more different, finding light in each other.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
curatorNote: A classic Victorian romance and coming-of-age story about an orphaned governess who faces hardship, solitude, and passion at Thornfield Hall.
whyFits: Jane's fierce independence, moral courage, and search for belonging make this timeless novel essential reading.
excerpt: Jane Eyre is a young woman who was orphaned at a very young age. Her fate seemed normal and without much excitement, but her life takes an unexpected turn when she is hired as a governess in Thornfield Hall.
There she meets the enigmatic Mr. Rochester. A series of strange and haunting events begin to take place, while at the same time a deep love begins to bloom between them.
In this classic novel, we witness how a woman develops her capacity to love and how, despite life's immense adversities and secrets, dignity and devotion survive.

title: Red Rising
author: Pierce Brown
curatorNote: A thrilling sci-fi dystopian tale of Darrow, a Helldiver of Mars, who infiltrates the ruling Gold caste to bring down a tyrannical hierarchy from within.
whyFits: High-stakes action, fierce loyalty, and the struggle for justice on a terraformed Mars.
excerpt: Darrow is a Red, a member of the lowest caste in the color-coded society of the future. Like his fellow Reds, he works all day, believing that he and his people are making the surface of Mars livable for future generations.
Yet he discovers he and his kind have been betrayed. Humanity reached the surface generations ago, and the Reds are nothing more than slaves to a decadent ruling class of Golds.
Driven by memory and a longing for justice, Darrow sacrifices everything to infiltrate the Institute where the dominant Gold caste competes for power.

title: The Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
curatorNote: Kafka's famous surreal novella about Gregor Samsa, a traveling salesman who wakes up one morning transformed into a monstrous insect.
whyFits: A profound exploration of isolation, family duty, and the human condition wrapped in a haunting allegory.
excerpt: One morning, when Gregor Samsa woke from troubled dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a horrible vermin. He lay on his armour-like back, and if he lifted his head a little he could see his brown belly.

Gregor was a traveling salesman whose income supported his entire family. All the events unleashed from this strange phenomenon create a growing narrative tension that does not cease until the end of the story.
As Gregor tries to navigate his new reality inside his room, his family struggles between pity, disgust, and the harsh pressures of everyday survival.

title: The Power of Concentration
author: Theron Q. Dumont
curatorNote: A classic guide written in 1918 offering lessons on mental focus, self-mastery, willpower, and quiet mental poise.
whyFits: Great for sharpening focus and cultivating quiet mental clarity during quiet study hours.
excerpt: Concentration finds the way. It is the key to mental mastery, allowing you to focus your mind's scattered energy onto a single goal until obstacles give way.
The person who can concentrate can command their own attention, quiet unwanted thoughts, and channel their willpower toward constructive action in business and personal life.
Concentration gives mental poise. Through daily practice of steady attention, you develop an inner calm and confidence that remains steadfast even amidst surrounding turmoil.

title: White Nights
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
curatorNote: A poignant sentimental story set during four magical Saint Petersburg summer nights, where a lonely narrator meets Nastenka.
whyFits: Captures the delicate beauty of fleeting encounters, late-night walks, and quiet romantic longing.
excerpt: The story takes place during four white nights in Saint Petersburg—a natural phenomenon where twilight lasts all night. The narrator, a lonely dreamer who wanders the city streets, meets Nastenka crying on a bridge.
After defending her from a harasser, Nastenka agrees to meet him each night as a friend, on the sole condition that he must not fall in love with her.
Over four quiet nights under the dim northern sky, they share their deepest secrets and longings, creating a fragile bond of romance and heartfelt melancholy.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
curatorNote: A dark, wild masterpiece of love, obsession, and revenge set on the bleak Yorkshire moors between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw.
whyFits: Atmospheric and intense, echoing the stormy, mist-covered heights of mountain landscapes.
excerpt: When Mr. Earnshaw brings the orphaned Heathcliff home to Wuthering Heights, he sparks an intense relationship between Heathcliff and his daughter Catherine, as well as fierce hatred from her brother Hindley.
Heathcliff and Catherine share an unspoken, almost mystical connection amidst the windy moors, but social pressures and misunderstandings force them apart.
Jealousy, revenge, and passion interweave against the cloudy and cold landscape, reflecting the tormented psychology of the characters across generations.
